frequency_question: How often does a structural relaxation of blocked input tax credits on immovable property occur within a 4-year window across major GST/VAT jurisdictions?
membership_rule: Members are national tax jurisdictions with a comprehensive Goods and Services Tax or Value Added Tax featuring explicit statutory blocks on input tax credit for immovable property construction, observed over any rolling 4-year period since 2000.

cases.name: EU VAT Directive member state adjustments on real estate capital goods adjustments (e.g., Spain 2012 reforms)
South Africa VAT Act amendments regarding fixed property input deductions
Australia GST Act provisions on commercial property developments
Canada Excise Tax Act provincial harmonizations (Ontario/BC)
New Zealand Goods and Services Tax Act land and property rule overhauls
India GST regime initial implementation and subsequent review windows

coverage_note: 6 named jurisdictions representing major VAT/GST frameworks; believed representative of global tax legislative behavior for blocked credit reviews.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller developing economies without mature VAT frameworks.
skeleton: 6 distinct national tax jurisdiction review windows x 1 structural reform instance
validity_reason: Tax legislative rigidity and reform cycles evolve slowly over decades, keeping structural base rates stable through the end of the decade.
